title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is an impersonation case built on synthetic media. A fake Facebook profile was used to make contact, a video call was used to capture the victim, and AI-generated explicit videos were used as the threat material. The AI component sits at the coercion stage, not at the contact stage: the recorded call supplied the leverage, and generated video was allegedly used to widen it.

The failure is not a model error or a system running outside its design conditions. It is a person using generative tools to manufacture compromising material and pass it off as real, which is the harm deepfake capability makes cheap. Catching it would have required platform-level detection of the fake profile before contact, or forensic examination of the generated videos once the demand was made. Neither is described in the reporting as having happened before the victim went to the cybercrime team.

What is established is that four people were arrested and that police linked the accused's number to prior complaints and found material on their phones. What is not established is guilt, intent, or the authenticity of any specific video, since an arrest is not a conviction and the allegations have not been tested in court.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student and three associates were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI using AI-generated explicit videos. Police said Md Faisal, 22, a second-year BCom student, and Md Amaan Tyagi, Md Hammad Tyagi and Md Faizaan Malik created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim in a compromising position during a video call on Sept 10, then demanded $50,000 and threatened to circulate the footage and AI-made obscene videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on Sept 17.

Police found the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints, and their phones revealed AI sextortion videos and links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore. The gang had been active since 2023 and allegedly cheated hundreds of people in India and abroad. Four members were arrested on Friday, while some accomplices, including Maroof, remain absconding.
